PRESENTATION: Premium professional film-production character bible / modeling reference sheet. Clean editorial layout. Neutral studio background. Soft realistic studio lighting. Sharp facial details. Natural skin pores and texture. Individual hair strands. Realistic fabric and accessories. Accurate human anatomy. Consistent camera perspective. Clean thin borders between panels. Professional labels underneath each view. Minimal elegant typography. High-end fashion / model reference aesthetic.

PHOTOREALISM: Ultra-photorealistic. Real human appearance. Natural skin texture. Realistic eyes. Physically accurate hair. Natural shadows. Realistic proportions. No CGI appearance. No plastic skin. No doll-like face. No artificial beauty-face replacement.

NEGATIVE PROMPT: different person, different face, face morphing, identity drift, altered facial structure, different eyes, different nose, different lips, different jawline, different skin tone, different hairstyle, inconsistent body proportions, duplicate person, distorted anatomy, asymmetrical face, plastic skin, waxy skin, CGI, 3D render, cartoon, anime, illustration, over-beautification, excessive makeup, unrealistic eyes, blurry face, low detail, extra fingers, missing fingers, malformed hands, bad anatomy.

OUTPUT: One complete, highly detailed professional CHARACTER CONSISTENCY SHEET in a single image, suitable as a master reference for generating consistent images and videos of this character.

Video created by Seedance 2.5:

SCENE: A day in New York shot entirely by the subject herself: waking in her hotel suite, coffee, getting ready, out into the city, back to the room at night.

ACTIVE REFERENCES: @image1 — the hotel suite. Curved cove ceiling with warm LED coving, deep red carpet, cream walls, two black organic sculptures above a light wood headboard, white bedding with red pillows, twin bedside lamps, pale sofa, oval coffee table, sheer curtains, dark door. @image2 — the subject. Young woman, shoulder-length wavy blonde hair with curtain bangs and highlights, light freckles, thin gold necklace, silver ring, dark brown off-the-shoulder knit with white diamond-stripe pattern. 100% matches the reference.

CAMERA OWNERSHIP LOCK: Only two positions exist. HELD: arm extended, camera 0.4–0.7m from her face, visible arm tension, tilt and step-bounce. PROPPED: camera on a surface she placed it on, crooked and fixed, with her moving in and out of frame. No operator shots, no tracking, nothing she could not have filmed alone.

FORMAT: Eight shots, 30s, seven hard cuts, no fades. Real-time.

0–4s SHOT 1 — PROPPED, morning room. Camera on the sideboard 3m from the bed at 1.1m, static and tilted. The suite matches @image1: cove light on, curtains half open, cool daylight across the red carpet. @image2 is visible at 0.0s, sitting up on the bed edge. She rubs her face and says to the running camera: “It’s seven. In New York. Why am I awake.” She stands and walks out screen-right. HARD CUT.

4–7s SHOT 2 — HELD, window light. Arm’s length, above eye line. She pulls the curtain, squints at the street below, then looks into the lens: “Okay. It’s actually happening.” Arm wobble throughout. HARD CUT.

7–11s SHOT 3 — PROPPED, coffee. Camera on the oval coffee table, low, looking up past a cup. She sits into frame, pours, tastes, and says: “Hotel coffee. We’ll fix that outside.” Steam bends in the light. HARD CUT.

11–15s SHOT 4 — HELD, mirror. Camera at chest height reflected in the suite mirror. She works through her hair with the other hand. At 13s: “This is as good as it gets. Let’s go.” HARD CUT.

15–18s SHOT 5 — HELD, leaving. Camera held low at waist height, turned forward. She crosses the red carpet to the door. She opens it and corridor light floods the frame. Off-frame: “Downtown first.” HARD CUT.

18–22s SHOT 6 — PROPPED, street. Camera on a stoop rail, static and crooked. A New York block behind her: brownstone steps, fire escapes, yellow cabs, steam from a vent. She walks in from screen-left, stands in frame, and says: “Look at this street.” Then walks to the lens and takes it. Passers-by cross the foreground. HARD CUT.

22–26s SHOT 7 — PROPPED, diner. Camera on the counter behind a plate, looking up. She sits into frame, takes a bite, eyes widen, and says: “Okay, that’s the one.” She laughs and keeps eating. HARD CUT.

26–30s SHOT 8 — HELD, night, back in the room. She lies back across the white bedding, hair spread, in the brown knit again. Bedside lamps and cove light are the only sources. Into the lens: “Twenty thousand steps. Everything hurts.” Softer: “Same time tomorrow.” She waves as she lowers the camera. 30.0s black.

SPEECH: Only the quoted lines are spoken, at the timings given, all in her voice. Lips still at all other times. No voiceover, no second speaker, no offscreen voices. Delivery is casual, unrehearsed, mid-breath, sometimes trailing off.

CONTINUITY: The suite matches @image1 in both interior sequences. Hair, necklace, ring, face, body proportions, and outfit details remain identical throughout.

PHYSICS: Loose knit slides on the shoulder with every arm movement. Wavy hair lags a frame behind head turns. Bedding creases under her weight. Step energy is visible in every HELD frame.

LIGHTING: Shots 1–4 use cool daylight from the curtains as key and warm cove LED as fill. Shot 5 uses corridor light. Shots 6–7 use hard street daylight and warm diner practicals. Shot 8 uses lamps and cove light only.

AUDIO: Diegetic only, from the same camera — room tone, footsteps, door, traffic, sirens, steam vents, diner clatter, and wind. Ambience ducks under her lines. No music.

LOCKS: Photoreal live action, 4K detail, fine grain, warm consumer-camera color, mild rolling shutter and auto-exposure hunting. She is the only person who speaks. Background figures are anonymous and unfocused. No subtitles.

title: GTA 6 is just around the corner, and today we got a…
prompt:
# GTA VI — LUCIA'S WARDROBE CUSTOMIZATION

## REFERENCE IMAGES — STRICT CHARACTER AND UI GUIDANCE

Use all four provided reference images according to their specific purposes.

@Image1 — LUCIA'S FACE
Use Reference 1 as a primary identity reference for Lucia's facial features. Preserve her recognizable face, facial structure, eyes, nose, lips, and overall identity throughout the entire video.

@Image2 — LUCIA'S FACE FROM ANOTHER ANGLE
Use Reference 2 as an additional identity reference to ensure that Lucia's face remains consistent when viewed from different camera angles. Combine References 1 and 2 to establish a stable, recognizable character identity.

@Image3 — LUCIA'S APPEARANCE AND HAIRSTYLE
Use Reference 3 as the definitive reference for Lucia's hairstyle. Reproduce this hairstyle as accurately as possible, including its shape, length, color, texture, and styling.

Lucia's hairstyle must remain absolutely unchanged throughout the entire video, including every outfit transition and camera change. Never restyle, shorten, lengthen, recolor, or otherwise modify her hair.

 — GTA-STYLE MINIMAP
Use Reference 4 as the visual reference for the in-game minimap displayed in the bottom-left corner during the initial third-person gameplay sequence.

Match the minimap's general appearance, shape, placement, proportions, colors, road layout style, and visual treatment as closely as possible.

Reference 4 is specifically for the minimap UI, not for Lucia's appearance or the environment.

Do not display the minimap during the frontal wardrobe customization sequence.

---

## SCENE 1 — THIRD-PERSON GAMEPLAY

Create a highly realistic GTA VI gameplay-style video featuring Lucia, an adult female protagonist from Grand Theft Auto VI.

The footage must resemble genuine real-time gameplay captured directly from a modern Grand Theft Auto game. Use realistic in-game character rendering, detailed environmental textures, natural character animation, and the recognizable visual language of GTA VI.

The opening shot uses a classic third-person gameplay camera positioned behind Lucia at a natural video game camera height.

Lucia walks naturally through a stylish modern Vice City apartment toward an open walk-in wardrobe.

She wears tight black, high-waisted leggings that accentuate her feminine, curvy, athletic silhouette, along with a fitted cropped top.

Her silhouette should remain natural, attractive, and consistent with the character references.

### GAMEPLAY HUD

During this initial third-person sequence, display a GTA VI-inspired gameplay HUD.

**Minimap:**
A circular or rounded minimap is positioned in the bottom-left corner of the screen, matching Reference 4. It resembles an authentic in-game navigation map, with streets, road outlines, a player-position marker, and a clean, recognizable GTA-style presentation.

**Health bar:**
Display a small, clean health indicator in the lower-left HUD area, positioned and styled consistently with the game's interface.

Both the minimap and health indicator must remain visible throughout the initial third-person gameplay sequence.

The HUD must look like a native part of the game rather than an external video overlay.

### WARDROBE ENVIRONMENT

Lucia approaches a stylish walk-in wardrobe in the apartment.

The wardrobe entrance is decorated with distinctive pink neon lighting inspired by the original Grand Theft Auto: Vice City aesthetic.

Pink neon tubes illuminate the wardrobe entrance and cast a subtle pink glow onto the nearby walls, furniture, and floor.

The neon lighting evokes the iconic Vice City atmosphere while remaining believable within the realistic GTA VI visual style.

The pink illumination should be clearly visible when Lucia approaches the wardrobe from behind.

Lucia walks into the wardrobe and stops.

Throughout this scene, the camera follows her smoothly from behind, maintaining the standard GTA third-person perspective.

The minimap and health indicator remain visible until the camera transition begins.

---

## SCENE 2 — CAMERA SWITCH AND WARDROBE CUSTOMIZATION

As Lucia enters the wardrobe and stops, the camera performs a clean, deliberate cut to a frontal, nearly full-body view.

Lucia is now standing inside the wardrobe, facing directly toward the player.

Her entire body and current outfit remain visible. The pink neon glow from the wardrobe entrance contributes to the atmosphere in the background.

The camera is stationary, resembling a genuine in-game character customization screen.

### CRITICAL HUD TRANSITION

The moment the camera switches from the third-person rear view to the frontal wardrobe customization view, the gameplay HUD disappears completely.

The minimap vanishes.

The health indicator vanishes.

Neither the minimap nor the health indicator may remain visible, reappear, or overlap with the clothing selection interface during the frontal customization sequence.

The only interface visible during this sequence is the dedicated clothing selection menu described below.

The transition should feel intentional and authentic, as if the game has entered a wardrobe customization mode.

---

## SCENE 3 — CLOTHING SELECTION INTERFACE

A polished GTA VI-inspired wardrobe interface appears along the bottom portion of the screen.

Five large horizontal rectangular clothing tiles are arranged in a single row, extending from the left edge toward the right edge of the screen.

The tiles are large enough for their outfit previews and labels to remain clearly recognizable.

Each tile contains:

* A miniature preview of Lucia wearing the corresponding outfit.
* The outfit name in clean, legible white text.
* A dark, subtly translucent background.
* Consistent dimensions and spacing.

The currently selected tile has a bright, distinctive pink selection border inspired by the Vice City color palette.

The active tile is slightly brighter than the other tiles. Inactive tiles remain visible but are less prominent.

The selection interface should resemble a premium modern open-world game UI, with restrained gradients, subtle highlights, clean typography, and smooth selection animations.

The interface remains fixed at the bottom of the screen.

Lucia stands in the center of the frame, facing the camera. Her face, hairstyle, body proportions, pose, and position remain consistent throughout the entire sequence.

---

## SCENE 4 — OUTFIT SELECTION AND INSTANT CLOTHING CHANGES

The active selection moves from the first tile to the next, one tile at a time.

Every selection change triggers a short, crisp, satisfying video game UI click.

At the exact moment of each click, the pink selection border moves to the newly selected tile, and Lucia's clothing instantly changes to match that tile's outfit preview.

The outfit change must feel like a real-time in-game wardrobe mechanic.

The clothing switches instantly and cleanly. There is no gradual morphing, no melting fabric, no intermediate outfits, and no changes to Lucia's body.

### SLOT 01 — VICE CITY HEAT

**Outfit preview:** Lucia wearing a fitted red mini dress.

The dress features thin straps, a deep V-shaped neckline, and a short hemline above the knees.

The material looks realistic, with natural folds and a flattering fitted silhouette.

When Slot 01 becomes active, Lucia immediately wears this exact red dress.

### SLOT 02 — MIDNIGHT LATEX

**Outfit preview:** Lucia wearing a sleek, glossy black latex bodysuit.

The outfit features long sleeves, a fitted silhouette, and a front zipper.

The black latex reflects the ambient pink neon lighting with realistic, controlled highlights.

The outfit is fashionable, bold, and form-fitting.

When Slot 02 becomes active, Lucia immediately wears this exact black latex outfit.

### SLOT 03 — NEON TROUBLE

**Outfit preview:** Lucia wearing a short black high-waisted skirt, a fitted cropped top, and tall black boots.

The skirt has a modern, fashionable cut. The cropped top is fitted and reveals her midriff.

The boots complement the outfit's edgy Vice City nightlife aesthetic.

When Slot 03 becomes active, Lucia immediately wears this exact outfit.

### SLOT 04 — TOMMY'S LEGACY

**Outfit preview:** Lucia wearing a feminine, modern reinterpretation of Tommy Vercetti's iconic outfit from the original Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

The defining element is a colorful, short-sleeved Hawaiian shirt inspired by Tommy Vercetti's recognizable tropical shirt.

However, the shirt is tied in a knot at the front, just above the waist, leaving Lucia's midriff clearly visible.

The shirt retains the original Vice City-inspired tropical aesthetic, including a bold, colorful pattern reminiscent of Tommy's iconic look.

She wears short blue denim shorts with visibly frayed, distressed hems.

The denim has realistic texture, stitching, and natural creases.

The overall outfit should immediately evoke the original Vice City while looking stylish and feminine on Lucia.

**Important:** This is a direct visual homage to Tommy Vercetti's iconic Hawaiian shirt, adapted into a tied-front crop shirt and paired with short, frayed denim shorts.

When Slot 04 becomes active, Lucia immediately wears this exact outfit.

### SLOT 05 — VICE BEACH

**Outfit preview:** Lucia wearing a fashionable red one-piece swimsuit.

The swimsuit features a plunging neckline, an open back, and high-cut legs.

The design is sleek, elegant, and inspired by the vibrant beach culture of Vice City.

The material has realistic fabric texture and natural highlights.

When Slot 05 becomes active, Lucia immediately wears this exact swimsuit.

---

## SCENE 5 — AUDIO AND ATMOSPHERE

Throughout the entire video, include subtle environmental audio that makes the apartment feel lived-in.

A radio is playing somewhere in the apartment, slightly away from the camera.

The music sounds as though it is coming from a real radio speaker in another room.

It should have a slightly distant, room-filtered quality, with the sound naturally blending into the environment.

Use an original, non-identifiable background music track inspired by the atmosphere of an upbeat 1980s Miami and Vice City radio station.

The music should feel stylish, summery, and slightly nostalgic.

It must remain in the background rather than overpowering the scene.

During the wardrobe customization sequence, the radio continues playing uninterrupted.

Every time the active clothing tile changes, a short, crisp, recognizable video game UI click is heard clearly over the background music.

The clicks must be synchronized precisely with the visual selection changes.

Do not add dialogue, narration, or unnecessary sound effects.

---

## VISUAL CONSISTENCY — ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENTS

**CHARACTER IDENTITY**
Lucia must remain recognizable and consistent with References 1, 2, and 3.

**HAIRSTYLE**
Reference 3 defines Lucia's hairstyle. Her hair must remain identical in every shot and with every outfit.

**OUTFIT-TO-THUMBNAIL MATCHING**
The active tile's miniature preview must correspond exactly to the outfit currently worn by Lucia.

Every outfit change must be synchronized with the selection click.

**BODY AND POSE**
Lucia's body proportions, facial features, skin tone, and overall appearance must remain stable. Only her clothing changes.

**CAMERA**
The initial sequence uses a third-person camera behind Lucia. After she enters the wardrobe, the camera cuts to a stationary frontal view and remains there throughout the customization sequence.

**HUD**
The minimap and health indicator appear only during the initial third-person gameplay. Both disappear completely when the frontal wardrobe view begins.

**ENVIRONMENT**
The wardrobe, furniture, lighting, and background remain consistent during the customization sequence. The pink Vice City-inspired neon lighting remains part of the environment.

**UI**
Exactly five clothing tiles appear in a single horizontal row. The interface remains stable and readable. The pink selection highlight moves sequentially from one tile to the next.

**AUDIO**
Background radio music continues throughout the video. Every clothing selection produces a synchronized UI click.

---

## FINAL RESULT

The finished video should resemble a genuine GTA VI gameplay capture demonstrating Lucia's wardrobe customization system.

The opening establishes the authentic third-person gameplay perspective, including the minimap and health indicator.

The pink neon-lit wardrobe entrance creates a distinctive Vice City atmosphere.

The camera then switches to a frontal character customization view, with the gameplay HUD disappearing completely.

Five stylish outfits are selected one by one through large, clearly visible clothing tiles. Every selection produces a satisfying UI click and an immediate, perfectly synchronized outfit change.

Lucia's identity, hairstyle, body proportions, camera position, and environment remain consistent throughout.

The result should feel like a polished, believable in-game feature rather than a conventional fashion video.

prompt:

Use the uploaded reference photograph directly in the upper 50% of the poster.

Allow only subtle, intelligent cropping around the outer edges when necessary, without compromising the main subject.

If required, naturally extend a small portion of the surrounding environment to fit the composition.

Do not redraw, illustrate, stretch, blur, or modify the subject's appearance, structure, or spatial relationships.

Do not introduce black borders, white margins, or empty edges.

2. BOTTOM HALF — MINIMALIST EDITORIAL ILLUSTRATION

Use a warm, near-white ivory paper background with an extremely subtle paper texture.

Analyze the main subject and visual story of the uploaded reference image.

Extract only the primary subject, preserving one or two essential identifying elements.

Transform the primary subject into a sophisticated black-ink editorial illustration.

ILLUSTRATION STYLE:

Avoid obvious hatching, scratches, architectural lines, or complex textures.

ILLUSTRATION SCALE AND COMPOSITION:

The illustrated subject must occupy approximately 72–77% of the canvas width and 58–64% of the bottom section's height.

3. COLOR RULES

The bottom illustration must follow a strictly black-and-white color palette by default.

Ordinary blue skies, green vegetation, stone surfaces, skin tones, and environmental colors must not be treated as accent colors.

2:3 vertical.

High-resolution, sharp, print-quality output.

Exactly 50% original reference photography on top.

No collages.

No combined images.
